text:
The Rangers lost Igor Shesterkin to a season-ending knee injury on Oct. 9, and it has not sunk them. Mike Sullivan's team is third in the Metropolitan, 13 of its first 22 games won, built on defending: they take 53% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets). Dylan Garand, waived before opening night, has made 15 of 23 starts. Tonight it's Joonas Korpisalo, healthy again after his own injury, with a .940 save rate in three games. Small sample, but a welcome one.

Injuries are the bigger test now. Pavel Dorofeyev, the summer's big acquisition, is on injured reserve (he practiced in a red noncontact jersey this week), and Oliver Bjorkstrand is out until late January. Will Cuylle has moved up beside J.T. Miller, and Tye Kartye has kept getting minutes. Miller, on a four-game point streak, is one assist from 500 for his career. And somewhere in all this, Glenn Gawdin scored his first two NHL goals against Vancouver and became the most written-about Ranger of the fortnight.

Buffalo is harder to read. The Sabres are 2-3-0 in their last five, losing the chance battle in those games (46%), but they scored six at Tampa on Saturday. The top line is cooking: Tage Thompson has goals in four straight (five in all), Zach Benson has six points in four, and Jiri Kulich has found his game between them. Benson is our sleeper for a point at 61%, because his line creates 3.97 expected goals per 60 minutes. Jack Quinn has goals in three straight. Our numbers flag all three wingers as due to cool, but the chances are real.

The question is the back end. Alex Lyon starts with a .890 save rate in four games, while Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen just picked up his 100th win. Buffalo also takes 4.1 penalties a game, and the Rangers have been one of the league's best penalty-killing teams. The playoff race says this matters more for Buffalo: 24% to the Rangers' 68%. Sam Carrick faces the Rangers for the first time since leaving them.
headline: Rangers keep finding goalies, Sabres keep finding goals
